en: Matthew 9

p.src: 1  He entered into a boat and crossed over, and came into his own city.

en: He entered into a boat and crossed over, and came into his own city.
u.src: 1  He entered into a boat and crossed over, and came into his own city.

p.src: 2  Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”

en: Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
u.src: 2  Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”

p.src: 3  Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”

en: Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”
u.src: 3  Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”

p.src: 4  Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?

en: Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?
u.src: 4  Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?

p.src: 5  For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk’?

en: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk’?
u.src: 5  For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk’?

p.src: 6  But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”

en: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”
u.src: 6  But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”

p.src: 7  He arose and departed to his house.

en: He arose and departed to his house.
u.src: 7  He arose and departed to his house.

p.src: 8  But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

en: But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
u.src: 8  But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

p.src: 9  As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.

en: As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
u.src: 9  As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.

p.src: 10  As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.

en: As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.
u.src: 10  As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.

p.src: 11  When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

en: When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
u.src: 11  When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

p.src: 12  When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

en: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
u.src: 12  When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

p.src: 13  But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

en: But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
u.src: 13  But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

9:13 Hosea 6:6

p.src: 14  Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”

en: Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”
u.src: 14  Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”

p.src: 15  Jesus said to them, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.

en: Jesus said to them, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.

p.src: 16  No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.

zh: 沒有人把新布補在舊衣服上；因為所補上的反帶壞了那衣服，破的就更大了。
en: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.
u.src: 16  No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.

p.src: 17  Neither do people put new wine into old wineskins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”

en: Neither do people put new wine into old wineskins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”
